deep.reconstruction:
Context: in E477 Euler studies the double series now written ζ(n,m) = Σ_{k>j≥1} 1/(k^n j^m), together with the variant that includes the diagonal j = k. He uses a symbolic shorthand. p^s q^t denotes the double sum with exponents s and t. p^w, with w = m+n the weight, denotes ζ(w). A bare p^j denotes the product ζ(j)ζ(w−j), so p^j and p^{w−j} are the same quantity. That identification is exactly what the next page exploits ('p^2, p^4 are equivalent to the odd p^9, p^7').

The tables give, for each odd weight, all double sums of that weight as rational multiples of ζ(w) plus integer combinations of products ζ(j)ζ(w−j).

The page starts by finishing §34. In weight 13 the p^2-coefficients are the binomial numbers C(11,k). The other columns, by contrast, come from the powers 8 and 6. Euler restores uniformity by splitting C(11,k) = C(10,k) + C(10,k−1): −1 + (10+1) − (45+10) + (120+45) − ...

He then writes out weight 15 in that form. Reading the printed table, the column of ζ(2j)ζ(15−2j) holds C(14−2j, k) + C(14−2j, k−(2j−1)), read from both ends. For example:
- p^2 column: (12+1), (66+12), ...
- p^4 column: (120+1), (210+10), ...
- p^6 column: (56+1), (28+8).

The odd columns p^3, p^5, p^7 hold short alternating binomial rows (2; 4,6,4; 6,15,20,15,6) at the top, mirrored with opposite sign at the bottom. A trailing +p^k on the lower rows supplies the diagonal/product term.

The ζ(15)-coefficients A, B, C, ... follow the recursion of the previous page, A = (15+1)/2 = 8. On the next page Euler gives them in closed form as ½(1 ± C(15,k)).

Check of the first row: Euler's classical sum is Σ H_n/n^14 = 8ζ(15) − Σ_{j=2}^{7} ζ(j)ζ(15−j). This matches q^14 = 8p^15 − p^2 − ... − p^7, the diagonal-inclusive convention.

§35 then announces how to remove the inductive character: replace the even powers by their odd partners, which gives a cleaner binomial layout. That layout is the general odd-weight reduction of double zeta values to products of single zetas.
errors: Euler's 'law' for weight 15 is explicitly inductive, extrapolated from weights 11 and 13; he says so himself in §35. No proof is given on this page.

Last term of row q^4: the transcription has +p^5. By the pattern (q^k gets +p^k for k ≤ 7), and by the corresponding rows for weights 11 and 13, it should be +p^4. This may be a printing or reading slip.
Last term of row q^2: the transcription has −p^2. The pattern and the weight-11/13 tables require +p^2.

ideas.what: Reduction of every double zeta value of odd weight (here weight 15) to ζ(15) and products ζ(j)ζ(15−j), with binomial-coefficient coefficients
ideas.modern_name: Euler's odd-weight reduction formula for double zeta values / Euler sums
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (E477, 1776); rigorous proofs by Borwein–Borwein–Girgensohn (1995) and Flajolet–Salvy (1998)

ideas.what: Splitting the binomial coefficients via Pascal's rule to make the columns uniform across orders
Symmetry p^j ≡ p^{w−j}, allowing even indices to be replaced by odd ones

deep.surprise_reason: This is the well-known odd-weight double zeta reduction from E477. It is extensively discussed in the modern multiple-zeta literature (Borwein–Bradley–Broadhurst, Flajolet–Salvy, and others) and credited to Euler. The page holds only a worked table for weight 15, nothing beyond that.
transcription_corrections: Row q^4: the final term, transcribed '+p^5', should read '+p^4' (compare the pattern and the weight-13 table).
Row q^2: the final term, transcribed '−p^2', should read '+p^2' (the image is unclear).
Row q^11: in the image the D is misread as ')'; it reads '−Dp^15'.
